messages:
kai: Quick question: should the loader expose a relaxed_consistency mode that lets mixed-epoch chunks be used during emergency fallback? Thinking about call-volume spikes + cross-region failover.
alyssa: That sounds dangerous but useful. What are the exact guarantees we offer in relaxed mode?
kai: Proposal: relaxed_consistency allows activation from mixed epochs only for read-only activations; writes (hotpatches) still require strict epoch pin. We also emit a heavy telemetry tag and rate-limit the number of mixed-epoch activations per model instance.
ram: We need clear semantics for KV cache + attention cache. If an activation uses mixed-epoch weights, cached KV must be invalidated on epoch switch to avoid silent inconsistency.
marie: Ops-wise, we must limit customer exposure. Rollout as feature-flag and require an explicit opt-in per-deployment. Also add an automatic revert: if verify_failures spike after enabling relaxed mode, flip back within 5m.
ishaan: From verification POV: allow quick-fingerprint accept, map mixed-epoch chunks, and continue full async verify. If a chunk fails full verify and it was from newer epoch, we should prefer rolling back to pinned epoch version and flag the activation for soft-fail.
nora: For public streams where index is missing, relaxed mode could reduce tail latency during storage hiccups, but how do we avoid serving content that later gets evicted?
kai: Two mitigations: 1) small time-to-live on mixed-epoch pages (eg 30s) unless they pass full verify, 2) disallow mixed-epoch usage for shards marked critical in shard metadata (critical: true).
ram: Also metricize it: mixed_epoch_activation_count, mixed_epoch_verify_failures, mixed_epoch_evictions. Add alerts when verify_failures/mixed_epoch_activation_count ratio > 0.01 over 1m.
marie: Add a guardrail: only enable relaxed_consistency for models with canary approval and a max concurrent mixed-epochs per host (eg 2). Make this configurable.
ishaan: API change: ModelHandle.open(manifest_ref, consistency=strict|progressive|relaxed). Default progressive. For relaxed we also require caller to provide a risk_ack token so users consciously opt in.
ora: UX suggestion: console should show a red badge when a model is running in relaxed mode and show how many activations are mixed-epoch. Customers need transparency.
warmupbot: Canary check: relaxed_consistency feature flagged in dedicated pool only; toggle recorded in audit log.
kai: Edgecases: if hotpatch overlay arrives and we have many mixed-epoch activations, we must avoid cascading evictions. Plan: upon overlay publish, mark new activations to prefer pinned epoch until mixed-epoch quota replenishes.
ishaan: For correctness, ensure callers can snapshot_epoch() and assert no mixed-epoch use during critical sections. snapshot_epoch should error if relaxed mode is on and mixed pages already present unless caller requests snapshot_strict().
ora: Testing: 1) simulate storage slowdowns and measure tail latency benefit; 2) inject corruption and confirm rollback triggers; 3) canary escalation test where we enable on small fleet and auto-disable on spike.
marie: Action items: kai write RFC-addendum with config knobs + default limits by EOD Thu; ishaan add verifier flow for mixed-epoch by Mon; ram wire metrics and alert rules by Tue; alyssa add console badge + opt-in UX by Wed; nora add e2e canary tests by next Fri.
kai: Thanks all. I'll draft the addendum and include a small flowchart for operators. Ping me if you want to pair on the verifier tests.
warmupbot: CI queued: relaxed-consistency/proto (6 tests).
